added: When electrical cables get moved around and bent a lot, sometimes the outer jacket can get ripped and expose the electrical wires inside. This situation is especially common with frequently used cables like phone and laptop chargers. If you see exposed wires in your electrical cables, fix them as soon as possible to prevent the problem from getting worse. Remember, always test exposed wires with a multimeter to confirm they’re not live, and wear insulated gloves and goggles to protect yourself from potential shocks.
===Fixing Exposed Electrical Wire with Electrical Tape===

#Stick electrical tape over the exposed wire and wrap it around once. Peel up the end from a [https://www.amazon.com/s?k=electrical+tape&crid=3VIC6CP3U2U0S&sprefix=electrical+tape%2Caps%2C153&ref=nb_sb_noss_1&tag=wikihow11950635-20 roll of electrical tape] and center it over the area of the cable with the exposed wire. Press it down on top of the exposed section and wrap it tightly around the damaged area.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref> This method works to repair minor damage in any type of electrical cable. [[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 1.jpg|center]]
#*Warning: Do not use duct tape or any other type of tape to cover exposed wire. Electrical tape is insulated and specially made for electrical applications.

#*Electrical tape comes in different colors, so you can try to find a color that most closely matches the cable you want to repair if you care about the aesthetics. Keep in mind that the electrical tape can get worn out and torn over time, so you might have to replace it eventually with a fresh layer.
===Fixing Exposed Electrical Wire with Sugru {{toc_item:With Sugru}} ===

#Open a packet of Sugru and knead the putty for about 30 seconds. Rip open a pack of single-use [https://www.amazon.com/Sugru-Tesa-Household-Everything-Personalizing/dp/B089WHGQDP?th=1&tag=wikihow11950635-20 Sugru] and pull out the silicone rubber putty. Squish it back and forth between your fingers for about 30 seconds to warm it up and make it more moldable.<ref>https://sugru.com/tech-gadget/how-to-repair-a-laptop-charger</ref>{{greenbox: '''Warning''': Do not use Sugru putty for high-voltage cables or DIY electrical work. Only use this method to fix exposed wires in low-voltage cables like electronic device chargers or headphone cords.<ref>https://sugru.com/tech-gadget/how-to-repair-a-laptop-charger</ref>}}[[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 4.jpg|center]]
#*Sugru is a moldable, adhesive silicone rubber putty that hardens into a rubber-like outer jacket when it cures.

#Roll the putty out into a long, thin rectangular shape. Place the putty on a flat surface and roll it back and forth with your fingers until it becomes long and thin. Press it down with your hand until it flattens into more of a rectangle so that you can wrap it around your cable.<ref>https://sugru.com/tech-gadget/how-to-repair-a-laptop-charger</ref>[[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Leave the putty to cure for at least 24 hours. Hang the cable up or lay it out on a flat surface somewhere out of the way. Leave it alone for a full 24 hours so the Sugru has time to cure completely.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref>[[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 7.jpg|center]]
#*The putty will turn into a strong, flexible protective casing around the exposed wire. The casing will help to prevent further damage to the area.
===Fixing Exposed Electrical Wire with Heat Shrink {{toc_item:With Heat Shrink}} ===

#Cut the heat-shrink tubing to be slightly longer than your damaged wire. Licensed electrician Marvin Woo explains that, “generally, the tubing should be just slightly larger in diameter than the wiring so that it can easily slip on and shrink tight enough when heated.”<ref>[v162030_b01]. 1 December 2021.</ref> Measure the damaged area and double the measurement just to give yourself plenty of material to work with. Cut the shrink wrap to size with scissors.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=odWOK8TaJEw&feature=youtu.be&t=92</ref>[[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Slide the heat-shrink tubing over the damaged spot and heat it. Woo instructs to “place the section of heat shrink over your wiring. Once in place, center yourself over the splice and apply heat using a heat gun to all sides of the tubing to evenly shrink it.”<ref>[v162030_b01]. 1 December 2021.</ref>[[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Don’t ever use an open flame to shrink heat-shrink tubing because you can easily melt it and damage your cable even more.

A comprehensive guide on repairing minor cable damage

When electrical cables get moved around and bent a lot, sometimes the outer jacket can get ripped and expose the electrical wires inside. This is especially common in frequently-used cables like phone and laptop chargers. If you see exposed wires in your electrical cables, fix them as soon as possible to prevent the problem from getting worse. Remember, always test exposed wires with a multimeter to confirm they’re not live, and wear insulated gloves and goggles to protect yourself from potential shocks.
==How to Fix Exposed Wires and Cables==

The best way to deal with minor damage on a wire is to sheathe it. You can do this with Sugru putty or heat shrink wrap, although the easiest and fastest option is usually to wrap the exposed wire with electrical tape.
===Electrical Tape===

#Stick electrical tape over the exposed wire and wrap it around once. Peel up the end from a [https://www.amazon.com/s?k=electrical+tape&crid=3VIC6CP3U2U0S&sprefix=electrical+tape%2Caps%2C153&ref=nb_sb_noss_1&##affiliate_article_id## roll of electrical tape] and center it over the area of the cable with the exposed wire. Press it down on top of the exposed section and wrap it tightly around the damaged area.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref>[[Image:Fix Exposed Electrical Wire Step 1.jpg|center]]{{celebritygreenbox:162861|When dealing with exposed wires, safety comes first. Always turn off the power at the breaker before attempting repairs. For minor damage, an electrician may use tape to insulate the wire. However, if the damage is severe, replacing part or all of the wire may be necessary. Working with electricity is dangerous, so it's often best to consult a professional to ensure repairs meet the code.}}
#*Warning: Do not use duct tape or any other type of tape to cover exposed wire. Electrical tape is insulated and specially made for electrical applications.}}
#*You can get electrical tape in different colors, so you can try to find a color that most closely matches the cable you want to repair if you care about the aesthetics.

added: [[Category:Electrical Maintenance]]

When electrical cables get moved around and bent a lot, sometimes the outer jacket  can get ripped and expose the electrical wires inside. This is especially common in frequently used cables like phone and laptop chargers. If you are starting to see exposed wires in your electrical cables, fix them as soon as possible to prevent the problem from getting worse. There are several methods you can use to repair most minor damage to your cables. If you have a cable that is extremely worn out and its electrical wires keep getting exposed because of new tears in the outer jacket, it’s probably best to replace it.
==Steps==
===Wrapping Minor Damage with Electrical Tape===

#Stick electrical tape over the exposed wire and wrap it around once. Peel up the end of the tape from a roll of electrical tape and center it over the area of the cable with the exposed wire. Stick it on top of the exposed section and wrap it tightly around the damaged area 1 full wrap.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/how-to/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref>{{greenbox: '''Warning''': Don’t use duct tape or any other type of tape to cover exposed wire. Electrical tape is insulated and specially made for electrical applications.}}
#*You can get electrical tape in different colors, so you can try to find a color that most closely matches the cable you want to repair.

#*This method works to repair minor damage in any type of electrical cable. Keep in mind that the electrical tape can get worn out and torn over time, so you might have to replace it eventually with a fresh layer.

#Wrap the tape tightly around the wire 2-3 more times and cut it. Continue to wrap the tape around the damaged area, directly on top of the first wrap you made. Cut or tear the tape when you complete 2-3 more full wraps and stick the end down.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/how-to/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref>
#*Wrapping the tape more than once will help this quick fix last longer and help prevent further damage to the cable.

#Make 3-4 wraps of tape on either side of the area you just wrapped. Stick the end of the electrical tape on the cable just to the side of the damaged area you already wrapped, overlapping it slightly with the first wrapped area. Wrap it around the cable 3-4 times, then cut or tear it. Repeat this for the other side of the first wrapped area.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/how-to/ways-to-protect-and-fix-cords-around-the-home/</ref>
#*Wrapping the undamaged areas of the cable to the side of the area with the exposed wire that you wrapped first will just help prevent further damage to the weakened area.
===Repairing Charger Cables with Sugru===

#Tear open a packet of Sugru and knead it for about 30 seconds. Rip open a pack of single-use Sugru and pull out the silicone rubber putty. Squish it back and forth between your fingers for about 30 seconds to warm it up and make it more moldable.<ref>https://sugru.com/tech-gadget/how-to-repair-a-laptop-charger</ref>{{greenbox: '''Warning''': Do not use Sugru putty for high-voltage cables or DIY electrical work. Only use this method to fix exposed wires in low-voltage cables like electronic device chargers.<ref>https://sugru.com/tech-gadget/how-to-repair-a-laptop-charger</ref>}}
#*Sugru is a type of moldable, adhesive silicone rubber putty that hardens into a rubber-like outer jacket when it cures.

#Roll the putty out into a long, thin rectangular shape. Place the putty on a flat surface and roll it back and forth with your fingers until it becomes long and thin. Press it down with your hand until it flattens into more of a rectangle, so you can wrap it around your cable.<ref>https://sugru.com/tech-gadget/how-to-repair-a-laptop-charger</ref>
#*A piece of Sugru that is about as long as the width of your hand will provide good coverage of the exposed wire and relieve strain on the cable to prevent further damage.

#Wrap the Sugru putty around the damaged area and smooth it out. Center the Sugru over the section of cable with the exposed wire and wrap it around the cable tightly. Press the edges of the putty together where they meet and firmly rub the Sugru with your fingertips to smooth out the seam and remove any fingerprints.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-qjS6WiyhI&feature=youtu.be&t=6</ref>

#*If the area you’re repairing is close to the wall adapter or power adapter end of the cable, make sure to press the Sugru right up against the power block or the charger plug to create a smooth-looking repair. You can shape it to make it look like a part of the cable.

#Let the putty cure for 24 hours. Hang the cable up or lay it out on a flat surface somewhere out of the way. Leave it alone for a full 24 hours, so the Sugru has time to cure completely.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/how-to/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref>
#*The putty will turn into a strong, flexible protective casing around the exposed wire. This will prevent further damage to the area.
===Applying Heat-Shrink Tubing to Electrical Wires===

#Choose heat-shrink tubing with a diameter barely greater than your cable. Select a diameter of heat-shrink tubing that will fit over your damaged cable without leaving a large gap between the cable and the tubing. This will allow the tubing to shrink onto the cable to fix the damaged area.<ref>https://www.cnet.com/how-to/5-easy-ways-to-fix-fraying-cables/</ref>
#*Heat-shrink tubing is a type of shrinkable plastic tubing that you can use to cover and insulate wires. You can use a hair dryer or heat gun to heat it up and shrink it.

#*Note that heat-shrink tubing won’t work for cables that have ends that are larger than the cable itself, like chargers, because you won’t be able to get the tubing over the large ends. This method works best if the electrical cable has 1 end that is the same diameter as the cable itself.
#*You can use this method to repair any type of electrical cable with exposed wires. Heat-shrink tubing can be used to repair long sections of exposed electrical wire as well.

#Cut the heat-shrink tubing to at least twice as long as the damaged area. Measure the damaged area and double the measurement. Measure out this length on your heat-shrink tubing and cut the tubing using scissors.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=odWOK8TaJEw&feature=youtu.be&t=92</ref>

#*The tubing will be about 10-15% shorter after you shrink it, so cutting it twice as long as the damaged area ensures it will cover the exposed wire and some of the cable on either side of the exposed section to prevent further damage.

#Slide the heat-shrink tubing over the damaged spot. Slip the tubing over the end of the cable and center it over the exposed wire. This will ensure it covers the damaged area and an equal amount of the undamaged cable on either side of it to reinforce the area.<ref>https://www.ifixit.com/Guide/How+to+Use+Heat+Shrink+Tubing/64041</ref>

#Heat the tubing using a heat gun or hair dryer until it shrinks. Turn a heat gun or a hair dryer on to high heat and hold the tip as close to the tubing as possible without touching it. Wave the heat gun or hair dryer back and forth along the length of the heat-shrink tubing until it shrinks tightly around the cable.<ref>https://www.ifixit.com/Guide/How+to+Use+Heat+Shrink+Tubing/64041</ref>
#*This will stiffen the damaged area and protect the exposed wire to prevent further wear and tear.
==Tips==
*You can take old worn out electrical cables, such as phone and laptop charges, to an electronic waste recycling center.<ref>https://www.popsci.com/prevent-frayed-cables/</ref>

*If you have to replace worn out electrical cables, try buying more durable types like cables with a braided outer jacket instead of the standard rubber jacket.<ref>https://www.popsci.com/prevent-frayed-cables/</ref>
==Warnings==
*If you leave electrical wire exposed, the wire itself can start to fray, which can eventually result in a faulty or completely broken wire.<ref>https://www.popsci.com/prevent-frayed-cables/</ref>

*Avoid buying laptop chargers made by third party manufacturers, which can damage your laptop. Always buy a replacement cable from your laptop’s manufacturer.<ref>https://www.popsci.com/prevent-frayed-cables/</ref>
==Things You’ll Need==
===Wrapping Minor Damage with Electrical Tape===
*Electrical tape
*Scissors (optional)
===Repairing Charger Cables with Sugru===
*Packet of Sugru
===Applying Heat-Shrink Tubing to Electrical Wires===
*Heat gun or hair dryer
*Heat-shrink tubing
*Scissors
